comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that ChEC-seq2 and ChIP-seq show complementary patterns for RNAPII (C3, C4, C26-C28, C35-C36, C52). OpenEval emphasizes the modeling support (C49-C51) for why ChIP-seq fails to detect promoter/UAS RNAPII. Peer reviewers affirm this as the central observation with no concerns raised. Peer result also includes C117 connecting to biochemical observations.

Perfect agreement on claims C29, C38-C39, C5. Both evaluations support that ChEC-seq2 and ChIP-seq signals correlate with nascent transcription (SLAM-seq), validating biological relevance of ChEC-seq2 detection at different genomic regions. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this through praise of the 'carefully crafted study.'

Both support claims C30-C31, C79-C82 about UAS-associated RNAPII and TFIIB-independent recruitment to UAS versus TFIIB-dependent promoter recruitment. OpenEval emphasizes the mechanistic validation through TFIIB depletion. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge. Peer result also includes C103 from the Gcn4 experiments.

Perfect agreement on claims C41-C45 regarding PIC component positioning relative to TATA boxes and consistency with structural studies. Both evaluations support the technical validity and spatial resolution of ChEC-seq2 for mapping PIC architecture.

Both support the modeling framework (C48-C51, C118) showing ChEC-seq2 patterns match expected kinetics while ChIP-seq patterns require unrealistic parameters. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of parameter combinations. Peer reviewers describe modeling as 'thoughtfully done' and providing 'convincing new insights.'

Both support the kinetic modeling development and validation (C6, C88-C90). OpenEval emphasizes the excellent fit to ChEC-seq2 data with published rate constants. Peer reviewers accept the modeling approach but Reviewer 1 requests additional validation beyond the modeling itself. Peer result also includes C91 and C130.

Perfect agreement on claims C64-C66 regarding the novel method for detecting phosphorylated RNAPII forms genome-wide using mintbodies. Both evaluations support the technical soundness and biological consistency of the CTD phosphorylation mapping data.

Perfect agreement on claims C67-C72 showing ChEC-seq2 detects biologically relevant transcriptional changes during ethanol stress. Both evaluations support the concordant changes across multiple proteins validated by SLAM-seq measurements.

Divergent evaluations on claims C56-C62 about elongation factors. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting unexpected promoter enrichment but accepting authors' explanations. Peer Reviewer 1 rates as UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that 'ChEC isn't optimal for detecting components of the elongation complex over coding regions' and questioning whether promoter signals reflect biology or technical limitation.

Both support claims C73-C78 regarding TFIIB depletion effects validated by SLAM-seq and ChEC-seq2. OpenEval emphasizes specific interpretable changes in PIC positioning. Peer reviewers accept the modeling showing adjustment of kinetic parameters agrees with ChEC data. Peer result also includes C92-C93, C132 about multiple rate changes.

Both support claims C83-C87 regarding Kin28 inhibition effects. OpenEval details expected loss of CTD phosphorylation and differential regional effects. Peer reviewers accept the modeling and use of Kin28 inhibition as internal control. Peer result also includes C94, C133 about RNAPII destabilization.

Both support claims C92-C93, C132 about TFIIB depletion modeling requiring multiple rate changes. OpenEval emphasizes the ensemble modeling approach strengthens conclusions. Peer reviewers accept that 'adjustment of kinetic parameters agree well with ChEC data' for perturbation analysis.

Both support claims C94, C133 about Kin28 inhibition modeling. OpenEval concludes Kin28 inhibition destabilizes RNAPII at promoters/UAS in addition to blocking initiation. Peer reviewers accept the modeling framework and expected decrease in CTD phosphorylation as validation.

Divergent evaluations on claims C97-C106 regarding Gcn4 genetic dissection. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong validation from ChEC-seq2, fitness defects, and transcriptional changes. Peer Reviewer 1 rates as UNCERTAIN, stating 'the effects are small and this proposal should be explored more completely in future studies.' Peer result also includes C7, C32, C107-C109, C129 about mechanistic model.

Both address Gcn4 mechanistic model (C32, C107-C109, C129). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing modeling distinguishes UAS recruitment from promoter stabilization. Peer reviewers express reservation about the strength of conclusions, with Reviewer 1 finding evidence suggestive but not conclusive due to small effect sizes.

Perfect agreement on claims C2, C24-C25, C110-C112 that ChEC-seq2 and ChIP-seq agree for most proteins tested (especially direct DNA-binding proteins). Both evaluations support this validation as important for establishing RNAPII differences are specific rather than general methodological artifact.

Perfect agreement on claims C131, C134 drawing general conclusions from modeling that multiple rate changes are needed to explain perturbation effects. Both evaluations support these conclusions as well-founded based on modeling of multiple perturbations and consistency with literature on PIC instability.

Both address claims C114-C116 about mechanistic explanations for ChIP vs ChEC differences. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are reasonable but speculative hypotheses without direct experimental tests. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, affirming the overarching conclusion that methods capture distinct regulatory events, though they focus more on the complementarity than specific mechanisms.

Both address claim C33 (summary conclusion). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on entire body of work. Peer reviewers also support, with editor stating 'ChEC-seq2 captures distinct regulatory events' and reviewers calling it 'valuable and complementary method.' Peer result also includes C114-C116 about mechanistic explanations.

Both address claim C91 about modeling inability to fit ChIP-seq data with realistic parameters. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with detailed supplementary analysis. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall modeling framework that is 'thoughtfully done,' though they focus more on the positive fit to ChEC-seq2 than the negative ChIP-seq result.

Both address claim C117 connecting ChEC-seq2 results to published biochemical observations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting it bridges gap between biochemical and genomic observations. Peer reviewers include this in their affirmation of the core finding about complementary patterns.
OpenEval rates claim C119 (about RNAPII-nucleosome interactions) as UNCERTAIN/SPECULATION. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific speculative hypothesis.

OpenEval rates claims C121-C124 (about elongation factor promoter functions and what ChEC-seq2 detects) as UNCERTAIN. While peer Reviewer 1 expresses concern about elongation factor patterns (see R7), there is no separate peer evaluation specifically addressing these mechanistic speculations.

OpenEval rates claims C1, C14-C15 (background on ChIP-seq as established method) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are contextual background claims not specifically evaluated by reviewers.

OpenEval rates claims C8-C13, C40, C46-C47, C53-C55 (established background on transcription mechanisms) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are literature-based background claims establishing conceptual framework.

OpenEval rates claims C16-C23 (published kinetic parameters and ChIP-seq observations) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are background claims from literature establishing motivation for the study.

OpenEval rates claims C95-C96, C125-C128 (background on NPC-chromatin interactions) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are literature-based background claims establishing context for Gcn4 experiments.

OpenEval rates claim C63 (published work on Mintbodies in mammalian cells) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this is a background citation establishing precedent for the approach.

OpenEval rates claims C135-C136 (literature supporting PIC instability) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these are citations providing independent validation of modeling conclusions.

OpenEval rates claim C113 (published examples of ChEC detecting sites missed by ChIP) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this is a background citation providing additional context.

OpenEval rates claim C37 (negative control showing low signal at repressed genes) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this control, though it validates specificity of ChEC-seq2 enrichment.
